newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peru rebels tell Spain some wounded in embassy.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels tell Spain some wounded in embassy.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas holding at least 200 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on Wednesday said there were wounded people inside and asked Spain to mediate to get medical supplies in, the Spanish foreign ministry said.
"They have asked Spain to ask Peru to allow medicines in for the wounded," the chief foreign ministry spokesman told Reuters.
No further information was immediately available in Madrid on who was wounded, how many or their condition.
But the Polish foreign ministry in Warsaw said the guerrillas had threatened to start shooting captives unless a doctor was sent to treat a wounded comrade.
Witnesses near the embassy in Lima earlier said one guerrilla had suffered a serious bullet wound in his leg.
The Spanish charge d'affaires in Lima, Estanislao de Grandes, who is among the hostages, was allowed to telephone a Spanish contact in Peru who conveyed the guerrillas' request, the spokesman said.
Spain conveyed their request to the Peruvian government.
"We asked to allow them to send medicines inside," the spokeman said.

Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar earlier called Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and asked him to avoid using military force in the standoff for fear it would lead to a massacre, Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said.
Aznar asked Fujimori to use psychological tactics to persuade the hostage-takers to stand down.

The hostages include high-ranking diplomats who had been at a reception to honour the Japanese emperor's birthday when guerrillas from the Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) attacked the ambassador's residence.
